decisions.reason: Although indoor air quality sensing is related to our module platform, two years without clear market presence and overlap with adjacent environmental sensors suggest limited commercially useful learning, so we would redeploy resources.
As the direct successor to an earlier voltage-measurement module, it builds on deep prior knowledge and stable customer needs, making continued support and refinement the more sensible choice.
The MQTT proxy fits our software, connectivity, and API-generation capabilities well enough that we can still learn from and improve it at relatively low cost, despite somewhat uncertain traction.
A CAN bus interface remains close to our embedded communication know-how and our customers' automation use cases, so our existing knowledge base supports keeping it in the platform.

A carbon dioxide sensor module sits squarely within our sensing portfolio and can be advanced through our established electronics, firmware, and documentation capabilities, so it should remain on the market.

The touch panel accessory is comparatively peripheral to our core sensing and control architecture, and the weak market signal means its released resources are better used on core modules and software.
